messages:
maya: Quick pass on compact dashboard charts — two main pain points: legend height pushing layouts and ambiguous axis units on tiny tiles.
jonah: Agreed. On 4-column views the legend above chart changes height per card and rows fall out of sync.
lia: What if we change legend to an overlay rail that collapses into a slim pill? When collapsed it doesn't affect chart height. Click expands into a scrollable overlay anchored to the card.
pat: Overlay rail works. Important: expansion must not steal layout focus unexpectedly. When user opens it with keyboard, move focus into the rail. When they close, return focus to the legend pill.
samir: For units, propose "condensed" (K, M) by default on compact tiles, with full-value revealed on hover/focus. Also add a user-preference: always show full values.
maya: Microcopy idea for the pill: label = "Series (N)"; tooltip = "Open series list"; screen-reader label = "Series list, N items, expandable".
jonah: Implementation nit: overlay should have a subtle backdrop to indicate layering but must be click-through on brightly colored cards. Use a 6% black overlay.
lia: Another copy thought: when a number is abbreviated show a visible affordance (e.g., caret) that reveals the raw value and exact unit on hover. For keyboard users, pressing Enter on the caret opens a small popover with the raw number.
pat: Renderer constraint: avoid per-point DOM updates for reveal. Popovers can read the underlying raw value from tooltip dataset attributes, but rendering dimming must be handled in canvas/shader via masks/uniform.
samir: Accessibility: add aria-describedby on tick labels referencing a hidden element that contains the full number. Example: aria-describedby="#tick-1234-full" with the full numeric string.
a11y-bot: Checklist: "legend pill accessible name includes count; collapse/expand uses aria-expanded; focus management on open/close; tick labels have aria-describedby for full values; popover triggers keyboard focus; overlay has role=dialog and aria-modal=false (non-blocking)".
maya: Smoothing & spike handling: propose two modes in the chart settings: "contextual smoothing" (preserve spike markers but smooth line) and "resample smoothing" (downsamples for perf). Add hint: "Contextual smoothing keeps spikes visible as markers."
jonah: Nice distinction. UI: small segmented control: Contextual | Off | Resample. Default = Contextual.
lia: Outlier UX: instead of changing axis auto-scale, dim outlier points and add a faint caret marker on the axis edge when a point is off-scale with tooltip "value beyond auto-scale: X; view raw".
pat: Dev: caret marker should be a single overlay layer so we don't need extra draw calls per point. Maintain a list of off-scale points and draw them in one pass.
samir: For keyboard/voice users, focusing an off-scale marker should announce: "data point dimmed by auto-scale, value X, percentile Y" and offer a control to toggle inclusion in scale.
a11y-bot: Add to checklist: "off-scale markers keyboard focusable; announcement format example; control to include point in scale is accessible via keyboard and has descriptive aria-labels".
maya: Action items: Lia to draft pill/popover microcopy + hidden aria examples; Samir to write announcement phrases and a11y test steps; Pat to outline renderer approach for caret and dimming; Jonah to spec overlay ARIA and focus behavior. I'll update Figma with a compact-card variant.
lia: Will post copy options in #design and a small Figma layer.
samir: I'll prepare a short a11y checklist that QA can run against the staging build.
pat: I'll open an infra note with a perf sketch for the single-pass caret + mask approach.
jonah: I'll prototype the overlay pill interaction and demo in the next sync.
maya: Thanks all  goal is to land the rail, unit affordance, and spike UX next sprint. :thumbsup:
